hypothesis: Static contiguous scanline assignment may improve row locality and reduce scheduling overhead compared with the prior cyclic static-row schedule, though it could balance vertically varying AO work less evenly than dynamic 64-pixel chunks. Both prior candidates were valid, with aggregate means of 0.46414 s for cyclic rows and 0.46135 s for dynamic chunks; those aggregates do not establish a per-configuration schedule advantage. A direct serial path avoids team overhead at one requested thread. Pixel-keyed SplitMix64 streams, initialized from one serial render-seed draw, should keep worker streams independent of schedule and thread count.
notes: Only src/candidate.cpp is changed. The serial drand48 draw seeds the render before parallel work; each pixel then owns a distinct hashed PRNG state and output triplet. No correctness or timing result is claimed here; the controller should validate all official configurations and record repeated timings.
transformations: Replace worker-side drand48 draws with one serial render-seed draw and a SplitMix64-derived stream keyed by linear pixel index.
Parallelize contiguous groups of scanlines with OpenMP schedule(static), bounded by num_threads(threads); retain a direct serial loop when threads is at most one.
Keep all primary-ray and 64 ambient-ray loop counts, existing ray math and per-pixel accumulation; each iteration writes only its own pixel triplet.
